displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that Christianity becomes reasonable when an independently constrained historical resurrection case is combined with antecedent theological context and a morally serious, non-evasive interpretation of disputed scripture.

novelty.explanation: Repairs the live case by integrating its historical, theological, and moral bridges while preserving their separate evidential obligations.

premises.text: Early appearance testimony should be disaggregated by date, source, dependence, witness type, and explanatory target before its cumulative force is assessed.

novelty.explanation: Repairs compressed source analysis in the participant's resurrection case using the strongest skeptical objection.

premises.text: Resurrection should be compared with conscious fabrication, individual and collective experiences, memory development, and legendary growth through explicit likelihood judgments rather than canonical labels.

novelty.explanation: Extends the Bayesian framework into a comparative evaluation of ordinary alternatives.

premises.text: Only expectations demonstrably antecedent to Christian narration should contribute to the theological prior or interpretation of resurrection.

novelty.explanation: Repairs the independence problem identified in the prophecy exchange.

premises.text: Defenses of biblical morality must interpret each disputed provision in its full legal and literary context while acknowledging any residual moral cost rather than appealing to context generically.

novelty.explanation: Repairs incomplete slavery and conquest reconciliations through full legal and literary context while acknowledging residual moral costs.

conclusion.text: If these historical, theological, and moral analyses converge without borrowing support from one another circularly, Christianity may be rationally preferred to the examined alternatives, though important interpretive and moral objections would remain.

novelty.explanation: Repairs the event-to-Christianity bridge by making the conclusion cumulative, conditional, and proportionate.

newArguments.title: Adversarial source partition
newArguments.text: Partition the resurrection evidence into minimally dependent clusters before combining it: early Pauline tradition, later narrative detail, hostile or neutral background evidence, and sociological evidence about proclamation and cost. Estimate what each cluster establishes without help from the others, then discount overlap explicitly. This method prevents multiple retellings of one tradition from masquerading as independent confirmation while allowing genuinely separate features to accumulate. A resurrection conclusion gains credibility only if several discounted clusters remain jointly more expected under that hypothesis than under the strongest ordinary alternative.

novelty.explanation: Introduces a source-partition and dependence-discounting method not articulated by either participant.

newArguments.title: Authority as calibrated corroboration
newArguments.text: A resurrection need not deductively entail every teaching to possess evidential relevance to authority. If Jesus publicly connected his mission, death, anticipated vindication, and moral teaching before the event, then a well-supported resurrection could corroborate that integrated self-understanding. The argument must therefore establish those antecedent connections independently and limit its conclusion to teachings sufficiently linked to the vindication claim. This answers the inferential-gap objection probabilistically while avoiding the claim that an extraordinary event validates unrelated propositions.

novelty.explanation: Repairs the missing bridge by narrowing corroboration to independently established antecedent claims.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that Christianity remains unestablished unless independent historical evidence supports resurrection, contextual evidence validly connects it to Christian authority, and disputed moral teachings survive direct ethical scrutiny.

novelty.explanation: Extends the skeptical route into a unified but disjunctive set of evidential and moral tests.

premises.text: Canonical status neither discredits nor authenticates a source; dating, provenance, dependence, genre, and corroboration must determine its historical weight.

novelty.explanation: Repairs the skeptical tendency to treat the biblical label as evidentially dispositive.

premises.text: Evidence of literary shaping weakens resurrection history only when it is connected specifically to the relevant appearance material and distinguished from ordinary literary presentation of remembered events.

novelty.explanation: Repairs overgeneralization from literary parallels to wholesale unreliability.

premises.text: Even strong resurrection evidence requires separately warranted premises linking the event to Jesus's identity, authority, and the particular doctrines under consideration.

novelty.explanation: Extends the central inferential-gap argument while acknowledging contextual probabilistic bridges.

premises.text: A perfect-goodness claim is vulnerable when a specific scriptural rule remains morally defective after its strongest contextual and regulatory interpretation is granted.

novelty.explanation: Extends the concrete slavery objection using a strongest-reading test.

conclusion.text: Unless Christianity meets all three burdens with independent and proportionate support, withholding assent remains justified, although that conclusion does not establish that every Christian claim is false.

novelty.explanation: Repairs possible overreach by distinguishing failure of establishment from comprehensive falsification.

newArguments.title: Cross-tradition evidential symmetry
newArguments.text: Apply the same source rules to Christian miracle reports and comparable claims from other traditions: similar discounts for insider testimony, literary dependence, theological motivation, temporal distance, and missing hostile corroboration. If the Christian case receives more favorable treatment, the difference must be justified by publicly accessible features rather than familiarity or doctrinal commitment. This symmetry test does not assume that every miracle claim is equally credible; it asks whether the method that elevates resurrection would also elevate structurally similar reports that the evaluator rejects.

novelty.explanation: Introduces a cross-tradition methodological symmetry test absent from the locked exchange.

newArguments.title: Residual wrong under strongest interpretation
newArguments.text: For each challenged moral text, first grant the most plausible historical, regulatory, and non-endorsing interpretation. Then identify the residual rule or commanded treatment that remains and ask whether a perfectly good legislator had morally preferable feasible alternatives. In the slavery exchange, release for specified injuries may mitigate abuse without explaining why other severe violence attracts no stated punishment when recovery follows. This approach avoids broad accusations and focuses the moral-authority challenge on what contextualization does not remove.

novelty.explanation: Repairs the broad moral indictment through a text-specific residual-wrong method.
